correctness.rationale: Every positive odd y satisfies y+3=2^j k with k odd, and the following odd iterate is ky; k=1 gives primitive j-cycle at y=2^j−3. For k≥3 a nonterminal arrival at 2^m−3 would force 2^m=2^jk²−3(k−1). Modulo three, m−j is even; since m>j, write m−j=2h and k>2^h, obtaining 2^j(k²−2^{2h})≥4k−2>3(k−1), contradiction. Therefore nonterminal odd values grow at least threefold and all intervening even iterates exceed the next odd value; full trajectories escape. Unique odd parts count bounded starts exactly, with leading 1/2(log2 X)^2. Independently tested numerous finite odd transitions and terminal predecessors.
